newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady as May driving awaited.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady as May driving awaited.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended steady on Monday in quiet activity that some traders suggested may be the calm before the stormy driving season that provides direction for the market.
Eurograde barges ended steady to up $2 at $194/$197 for prompt material. Traders said a 1,000 tonne barge traded at $197 for fob Rotterdam refinery material.
Cargoes were heard up $2 at $201/$205 cif for Eurograde, with a regular unleaded piece rumoured done at $195 cif into Hamburg, but this was not confirmed.
Swaps held onto their $2.50-$3.00 backwardation for May/June, which some traders said may entice inventory holders to sell into after recent contango.
"We assume that the driving season is starting in due course so there will be a kind of firmness, but it is very quiet," said one trader in Germany.
The arbitrage appeared open to the States for larger vessels but there was a lack of product to ship, he said.

Another trader said the cargo market will not put pressure on the barge market in the near term. Some alleged cargoes would alleviate any tightness in ARA caused by the recent buying spree of one player.

"The number of cargoes available for export are not really around," she said. "The cargo market has been pretty healthy and in that case it's not going to pressure the barges...It's highly possible for barges to trade at par with cif cargo (prices) in due time."
Traders said relatively rich gasoline crack spreads in ARA of near $5 a barrel may affect refinery production and sellers' intentions as the month of May approaches.
Another trader in Germany said local demand for stock material was muted, and not giving any prop to barges.
